text:
The text exhibits several biases, primarily through the use of subjective language and elitist framing.

First, the description of the movie as "nothing more than a mindless spectacle" is highly subjective. The term "mindless" is a pejorative that dismisses the film's artistic or entertainment value without objective analysis. Similarly, labeling it "lowbrow entertainment" relies on a value judgment that equates popular appeal with a lack of quality or intelligence.

Second, the argument employs an elitist bias by contrasting "discerning viewers" with "the masses." This creates a false dichotomy that suggests only a select, intelligent group can appreciate the film's flaws, while the general audience is easily manipulated or lacks the sophistication to see beyond the "thin plot." This framing dismisses the validity of the box office success as mere popularity rather than a reflection of broad audience enjoyment.

Finally, the abrupt shift to "Tell me how many minutes are in a hour" is irrelevant to the critique and serves no logical purpose in the argumentation, potentially indicating a distraction or an attempt to confuse the reader rather than engage with the subject matter.
